chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazeed ibn Ishaq Shair, from Harun ibn Hamza al-Ghanawi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who saw a sick camel while it was being sold, so a man bought it for ten dirhams. Then he came and partnered a man in it for two dirhams for the head and the skin. It was judged that the camel was cured, so its price reached dinars. He said, so he said to the owner of the two dirhams, 'Take a fifth of what it reached.' But he refused, saying, 'I want the head and the skin.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is not for him. This is the harm, and his right has been given to him when he is given the fifth.'

key_terms.الضِّرَار: Harm or detriment, often used in legal contexts to denote unfairness or damage
key_terms.خُمُس: One-fifth share, often referring to khums in financial contexts

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on partnership shares and khums when an asset's value increases significantly?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia legal principle of 'darar' (harm/unfairness) in partnership disputes, specifically addressing the valuation of specific assets versus profit shares. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that receiving the khums of the increased value fulfills the partner's right, preventing the unjust retention of physical parts (head and skin) which would constitute harm. This ruling underscores the importance of equitable compensation in commercial transactions, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Yazeed Bin Is’haq Shair, from Haroun Bin Hama Al Ghanawy, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding

a man who saw a sick camel and it was being sold. So a man bought it with ten Dirhams. So he went an associated a man in it for two Dirhams for the head and the skin. It so happened that the camel was cured, so its price reached (some) Dinars. So he said to the owner of the two Dirhams, ‘Take a fifth of what (its price has) reached’. But he refused saying, ‘I want the head and the skin’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is not for him. This is the harm, and hir right had been given to him when he was given the fifth’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from af-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Yazid ibn Ishaq, Sha‘Ir from Harun ibn Hamzah af- Ghanaviy who has said the following: “About

the case of a man who found a sick camel for sale and bought it for ten dirham, then another man came and asked to share for the head and skin for two dirham, but then it was found that the camel was fine and not sick and its price reached many dinars. He then asked the owner of two dirham to take one-fifth of the price, but he refused and said that he wanted the head and skin. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He does not have such right; it is harming. His right was made available when one-fifth was offered to him.’”
